_doc: Source of truth for the visual labels. apps: one object per App Store app id (layout, techniques, first_shot, quality, ai_smell, note). shots: per-image overrides (verified headline, language, note, exemplary). lite: image ids shipped in the lite package. See references/library-guide.md §5.

apps.note: Each shot takes one colour from the brand palette; 2-5 word headlines; one shot turns the feature list into tappable-looking chips instead of a paragraph.
Glossy AI-looking fantasy art and pink gradients; 'A Universe of Romance & Fantasy' could belong to any reading app.
Caps one-word hooks (1M+ NOVELS, BINGE) over the same purple and cover collages; interchangeable with every web-novel app.
Large left-aligned Turkish headlines with a cropped, tilted phone; conversational copy ('Okuduğun satırlar sohbete dönüşsün') though the first line is generic.
Strict orange/black brand system, alternates photo shots and UI shots; parallel headline rhythm 'Audiobooks you'll love. Podcasts you'll binge.'
One maroon background, one bolded key word per headline, award laurels on shot 1 and a matching cover collage closing the set.
Copy does the work: crossed-out 'DOOMSCROLL' and a screen time statistic as a hook; the flat grey background is forgettable.
Editorial feel: small coloured overline naming the feature + serif headline with one italic word; restrained navy/grey/cream palette.
Government-portal look: long Turkish headlines ending in '!', small type on a generic blue gradient, UI shown whole and unreadable.
Opens with a concrete number (1.6 million people a year) and a people cut-out; later headlines are small and wordy.
First shot spends itself on 'Your AI-Powered Collaboration Platform' with a sparkle icon; the rest list features one by one in long sentences.
Plain and small, but every shot follows the same believable business (a cake shop), so the UI content tells a story.
Pastel 3D blobs, floating tilted phones and 'all in one app' in low-contrast lilac text: the default AI-render look.
Quantified promise first ('Get hired 30% faster', with footnote); UI cards break out of the frame so the key element reads at thumbnail size.
Logo instead of captions, old device frames and 2016 dates: the store page says nothing about why to install.
Apple's house template: small black headline, light grey ground, whole-screen device. Clear but anonymous - fine for a utility, too quiet for a newcomer.
Bare screenshots with no captions; only works because the audience already knows the brand.
Bare screenshots, and the Turkish store shows a Spanish UI: an un-localised listing is visible to every visitor.
'AI intelligent service', 'Intelligent device configuration' and stiff translated sub-lines on a pastel gradient: reads as generated copy.
Consistent two-word imperative headlines (Create Instantly, Remix Anything, Play Together); the glossy 3D '#1 Platform' opener is the weakest shot.
Turkish headlines phrased as the user's own questions ('HANGİ KURUM KAÇ PUANLA KAPATTI?'), two-tone condensed caps; the paragraph under each headline is too long.
Every shot carries a headline, a sub-paragraph and a list of features; nothing reads at thumbnail size and the message is 'everything for everyone'.
Raw grade-book screens with no captions and old UI chrome.
Real lesson UI full-bleed, the caption sits at the bottom in a chunky coloured pill in the brand font; lowercase verb-led copy, one colour per shot.
Clean UI but no captions at all: the visitor has to work out the benefits alone.
Strong numbers (98% cheaper, 37 hours of speaking) but the chrome robot, flags and laurels on the opener are stock AI imagery.
Noun-phrase slogans (All-In-One Study Buddy, Pro-Level Explanation, Visual Study Agent) over UI that fades into white: generic and hard to read.
Dark-red glossy drama posters with slogans like 'Premium Immersive Drama Series' and 'Immersive HD Experience' - the category template, nothing ownable.
Same short-drama template (Watch Exclusive Stories, Diverse Content Selection) and a typo ('Onginals') left in a top-chart listing.
Distinct green brand pattern, one short Turkish promise ('Eğlenceyi yerinde yaşa.') and a phone that continues across shots 1-2; later shots have no captions.
Italic Title-Case slogans (Smooth Streaming, VIP Exclusive, Massive Variety of Short Dramas) and laurel numbers: generic category copy.
The app name is repeated as the headline on every shot; the real message is a tiny sub-line nobody reads at thumbnail size.
Strong brand colours wasted on filler pairs like 'Any Genre / Everything You Want' and 'Expect the Unexpected / Ultimate Emotional Journey'.
After a slogan opener, short concrete headlines on white with full-screen content (Find recipes for every season) let the content sell.
One sentence runs across all six shots with a spokesperson walking through them - clever, but it opens with 'is renewed', which is news for the bank, not the user.
Opens with 'We renewed the app for you!'; the remaining captions are small two-line instructions ('By adding your favorite menus to my shortcuts...').
Raw banking screens, no captions; balances and menus are unreadable at store size.
'Halkbank Mobil Yenilendi!' opener, then bottom captions with exclamation marks; like most Turkish banks it leads with its own redesign.
Warm brown ground matched to the dark UI, condensed headlines that are all verbs (Take a position on any outcome), a real athlete and a concrete offer on shot 1.
Brand circles in red/blue frame each shot; the credit-score shot (a giant 720 GOOD) shows how one zoomed number beats a whole screen.
Green/black/beige rotation, big left-aligned headlines with concrete numbers (Invest with as little as $1) and UI simplified to one card per shot.
Deep-blue system with bold white condensed headlines placed top or bottom as the UI needs; specific promises with footnotes (Earn 5% back, No late fees*).
Playful opener ('İndirim mmmmm' with a burger), then one-word Turkish category headlines (Yemek, Market, Su) on one green; partner logos pop out of the frame.
Concrete offer first (800 TL off your first 5 orders) and real courier/family photos - but the Turkish store gets English captions.
Turkish copy plays on the brand name ('Gelsin mi? Gelsin!') with highlighted words in pills; busy, but every shot states one concrete perk.
Starbucks green with star shapes and tilted phones; tidy, though English copy in the Turkish store.
Three shots, each one specific benefit with the payoff in bold ('Order ahead to save time (& avoid the line)'); the aside in brackets sounds human.
Condensed all-caps headlines on brand red with real products bursting out of the frame; the last shot completes the sentence ('OR WHATEVER THE DAY CALLS FOR').
Clean white with brand-red copy and a pun ('App-etite'); captions alternate top and bottom to leave room for the product photo.
Condensed blue caps and drink photography; the drive-thru photo on shot 1 shows the real moment of use.
Shots 1-4 solve one level step by step, so the rules teach themselves; the captions (Test Your IQ, Cute and Fun) are filler.
Eight near-identical gameplay frames with no captions; nothing changes from shot to shot.
One-verb headlines on a constant red banner (Collect! Fill orders! Renovate!) and a before/after shot that shows progress in one glance.
Single words as captions (RELAXING, SIMPLE FUN) over score screens - interchangeable with any block puzzle.
Verb-led caps captions in a bottom band (CLEAR THE BOARD!, BEAT THE CLOCK!) over real levels; key art saved for the last shot.
Same bottom-band formula; mixes plain puzzle frames with reward art so the set doesn't look repetitive.
Landscape key art with tiny corner captions: relies on the brand; in portrait search results these become thin strips.
Spec-sheet headlines (Multi-Reference Fusion, HDR Format Native 4K) on a teal gradient, with a typo ('Mutilingual'); reads like a feature list pasted into a template.
Google's plain template: small sentence-case headline over the whole dark UI; honest but undersells a visual product.
The before/after slider shows the value instantly; the Title-Case serif slogans (Trendy Themes, Designer-Grade Garden Decor) are interchangeable.
Stock-photo couples in collages and mostly no captions; '500+ Layouts' is the only real message.
Kawaii pastel world that matches the audience; consistent two-line imperative headlines (Make Your Battery Yours, Match Every Mood).
For a wallpaper app the product is the picture: most shots are just the lock screen with the wallpaper applied.
Five type sizes per shot, ellipses and exclamations ('WHEREVER YOU ARE, YOUR WORKOUT IS THERE!'); the eye has nowhere to land.
Decent bold-keyword headlines, but the Turkish store shows 'localised Australian foods' and 'Australians losing weight' - the wrong market's listing.
'Trusted by 300M women' opener, two-word headlines and zoomed UI cards with the one number that matters ('Period in 3 days').
Best Turkish copy in the set: short, spoken lines with a coloured second half ('Ne yediğini artık bil.', 'Ürün neyi saklıyor?'), placed top or bottom around a real scan.
Dark-to-orange brand gradient behind every device, award on shot 1, terse rhythm ('Lift it. Log it. See your gains.'); headlines are a bit small.
Giant 'PROGRESS STARTS HERE' opener and sentences continued across shots with ellipses; strong purple brand, uneven type sizes.
One lilac ground, a two-line headline with the key phrase in a white box (Predict your | next period) and UI cropped to the single card that proves it.
Neon-yellow opener with real press awards, then black shots with wide heavy caps and real coaches inside the UI: looks like a sports brand, not a template.
Seasonal refresh (a Halloween set: 'Embrace spooky season'), moody real photography and 3-word headlines; the content is the product, so it fills the frame.
Turkish captions with sub-brand badges and a racing-driver mascot; the rhythm 'Alırken, Satarken, Kullanırken' is good, but the type is too small for search results.
Rainbow gradients, floating bottles and 'DOA is here for you!' in English for a Turkish deposit scheme: generic and mis-localised.
Witty serif headlines with one italic word ('Attract people who actually get you', 'You wanted a sign, here's twelve') over real-looking people; every shot sounds like a person wrote it.
Clean and readable but generic: pale blue gradient, small headlines, a 'No.1 Wishlist app' laurel.
Title-Case headline plus one-sentence sub on dark gradients, with sticker-like UI fragments; the real party content keeps it human.
Magenta system with a small icon above each headline; the coverage comparison (93% vs 45%) is the one shot that persuades.
Channel grids with no captions; nothing says why this beats the TV remote.
Short Turkish imperatives (Haberi Hızlı Oku, İlanları Kaçırma) for a clear niche audience; the award laurels give no source.
Black ground with the key words in red; 'Get rid of clickbait headlines' names a real pain, unlike the generic 'Keep Up With The World' opener.
Heavy rounded Turkish caps (GÜNDEMİ TAKİP ET) on a new gradient each shot: bold and readable, but four shots repeat 'TAKİP ET'.
Editorial system: a small bold overline (Follow Today, Listen Today, Play Today) above a serif headline; each shot is one section of the paper.
Navy-to-red brand ground with short verb-led headlines; relies on live news content inside the device.
Every headline names a concrete job (Check your news blindspot, See the bias, factuality and ownership of any outlet) on a calm paper-beige ground; real award on shot 1.
Copy with a point of view ('Trade fear for faith in 5 minutes', 'Same headlines, different headspace') and a whole shot of short user quotes.
Shot 1 is the splash screen, shot 3 a login form: raw screens in capture order, no captions.
Tiny two-line captions on pale mint, a logo repeated on every shot; English copy for a Turkish appointment system.
Turkish government emergency app done carefully: consistent teal, a concrete headline per shot (Ses ve Data Yoksa Bile İletişimsiz Kalma), cards lifted out of the UI.
Long Turkish sentences, old device frames and dense forum text inside the screen.
Flat illustrated people in everyday scenes, one pastel per shot; warm and human, but the headlines are thin and low-contrast.
Plain pastel template, readable verb-led headlines; key cards (coupon, price) pop out of the screen.
An arch shape frames serif headlines over a warm grey; lifestyle photos alternate with UI. Pleasant, but the copy is generic (Save time, Be informed).
Navy ground with white serif headlines; 'Estimate costs to plan ahead' with a $2,151 estimate is the one concrete shot.
Stock models laughing at phones, 3D emoji stickers and broken Title-Case English (Share Amazing Sound With Friend).
Pink-on-green brand frame with caps headlines and one bold word each (CONNECT WITH FRIENDS...); content inside the UI is real and locale-specific.
Moody gradients sampled from the album art; captions are small but the photos carry the mood.
Bare UI states with small labels (Record from microphone, Play recording); describes buttons, not benefits.
Warm red-orange gradient that is the brand, light condensed serif headlines and the real prompt UI; 'Make any song you can imagine' says the whole app in one line.
Neon-lime glow, Title-Case slogans (Create Stunning AI Covers With Any Voice, AI-Powered Premium Song Recommendations): the AI-app template.
Google's white template with short verb-led headlines; works on brand recognition. The Turkish store shows London maps in English.
Each caption is a 4-6 line Turkish paragraph in small type; unreadable at store size - the clearest example of what not to do for a city-transit app.
A clever 'Go.more / Earn.more / Play.more' system ruined by tiny paragraphs and phones floating in empty white space.
Coloured transit lines run through every shot as the brand motif; key moments ('Your bus is arriving NOW', 'Significant DELAYS') pop out as tilted pills.
Flat cyan with bold dark headlines that each name a real driving moment ('Ditch the parking search stress', 'Stay informed with speed camera & police alerts').
Shell yellow everywhere, plain sentence headlines and full screens; on-brand but nothing pulled forward.
Shows the timer as a big number (15min, 2:19:59) instead of a whole screen; the icon-list shot is a cheap way to cover many features.
Black with 2-word headlines and a line icon above each (Reach anyone, Watch live); disciplined but cold.
Every shot a different loud colour, captions in white sticker strips, real (funny) posts as content: unmistakably the brand's voice.
Quiet beige and serif 2-3 word headlines that suit a writing platform; too quiet to stand out in search.
Clear two-colour headlines over a dark map, with a small honest disclaimer line on every shot ('Not an official report').
Strong typographic rhythm (one bold word + a lighter line: 'Restore / your old photos') on pure black; the content itself is AI portraits, so the set looks synthetic.
Small bold labels over vivid real effect results; the content carries it but 'Amazing templates' and 'Super transitions' say little.
Black template with real creator footage; plain verb-led captions ('Export in 4K with no watermark' is the only real differentiator).
One-word headlines (Create, Watch, Discover) with thin sub-lines on white; relies entirely on brand recognition.
Hand-drawn circles and arrows annotate the feature on each shot; looks human and points the eye exactly where the copy talks.
Snap-yellow ground, one-word bold headlines naming each tab (Chat, Lenses, Map); unmistakable brand, little persuasion.
Each headline names a concrete job with one word in brand blue ('Turn class notes into custom quizzes'); the UI shows that exact conversation.
Short two-line headlines and soft gradients sampled from the brand; every screen is a believable real prompt (translating a menu, a sleep routine).
Warm dark photography with serif headlines; the example prompts are localised per market (Cotswolds pub in the UK-English set, Miami Beach in the US).
Bold headline + thin sub, placed top or bottom around the UI; the Undo-send toast pulled out of the frame is the best shot.
Very specific examples in the UI (a field-trip form, a stroller under $320) but small headlines and a template-y blue fade.
Small two-line Turkish captions on grey, repeated headlines across shots and an old device frame; the only free signal is the official brand.
Calm dark green with real widget content and photography; captions are a little small but consistent.
Event app with a strong painted brand pattern, a small feature label above each headline and the key word in green; sub-lines are long.
Painterly AI-style mosque backdrops and serif Title-Case slogans ('Every Moment A Verse Every Verse Inner Peace'); heavy and samey.
Soft sage gradient and serif headlines; a whole shot given to one long user testimonial works better than any laurel.
Raw 2021 government screens with a carrier status bar; no captions.
Bare white UI screens with no captions or framing; disappears in search results.
Red hand-drawn loops tie the shots together, serif headlines put one word in italic ('No Ads or Purchases'), and a testimonial shot uses short real-sounding quotes.
Each shot introduces one sub-service by its logo with a short Turkish line; tidy, but the pastel gradients and small text are generic.
Heavy white Turkish headlines with concrete offers (Peşin Fiyatına 9 Taksit) for a 'Efsane Kasım' campaign; glossy 3D chrome hearts and bells add AI-render noise.
Colourful, with concrete numbers (Over 40,000 Products), but English captions on a Turkish grocery app with Turkish UI inside.
Pink-orange gradient with floating 3D hearts and stars; English caps captions in the Turkish store.
One teal ground, serif headlines with personality ('Don't wear it? Sell it!', 'Help old favorites find new love' spanning a garment) and real clothes.
Loud orange with a giant type poster opener; later shots are category labels (Women's Fashion, Home & Kitchen) - effective for its audience, not distinctive copy.
Concrete money everywhere ($10 bonus, coupons at 100,000 stores, 'You saved $9.52'), a review shot and real retailer logos: every claim is checkable.
Red brand ground alternating with real fashion photography; heavy white headlines lead with a money benefit ('Keep more of your cash with no selling fees').
Black ground, three-word headlines with one phrase in a hand-placed yellow highlight block (Join the | conversation); the UI shows believable posts.
A new saturated colour per shot with real-looking people and posts; the headlines are small for the amount of text.
One adjective per shot (Fast, Powerful, Private, Secure) with a one-line proof below; works because each word is the brand's real positioning, but the gradient template is generic.
'Simple. Reliable. Private.' as a three-beat opener, then bold-keyword headlines alternating brand green and off-white; the UI shows ordinary, warm conversations.
'Let's get real.' over a candid photo, then conversational blue headlines with product cards stuck onto real video frames.
Betting app: heavy italic Turkish caps on brand green-yellow, punchy but every shot shouts at the same volume.
Betting app: short Turkish caps labels (CANLI BAHİS, KUPONDAŞ) on flat yellow with sports balls; readable, feature-label copy.
Consistent navy caps headlines; 'USER-FRIENDLY EXPERIENCE' is filler, and English copy for a Turkish brand.
Betting app: glossy 3D balls, gems and glow on royal blue with stacked caps lists; noisy.
Betting app: condensed caps on a split green/black ground with required disclaimers; strong system, dense.
Fantasy sports: loud condensed type, purple-neon grids and offers; matches the audience but every shot is maximal.
Rounded blue cards with small Title-Case captions (Track Runners Seamlessly); real race content inside but nothing ownable.
Fantasy sports: condensed headlines with dog puns (Lettin' dogs out coast to coast) and a bright colour per shot; on-brand and energetic.
A green panorama across shots 1-3, then plain white shots with exclamation-mark sentences in English for a Turkish scooter app.
Flat brand yellow, condensed black headlines and one custom 3D object per service (burger, scooter, parcel); the 'Easy to...' copy repeats.
Red with a line icon above each verb-led headline; 'Get your bus ticket in 2 minutes' is the one concrete claim.
Small two-line captions with a yellow highlight box on pale blue; eight shots that look the same at thumbnail size.
Shots follow one ride in order (destination, ride, price, pickup, safety, rating) with a progress line on top; the 'GO ANY-WHERE' poster breaks the grid on shot 2.
Real riders in real cars behind each phone, with human two-beat lines ('Be there soon. Really soon.', 'Schedule ahead, leave stress behind').
Warm beige with a small brand illustration above each two-line headline; the real listing photos do the selling.
Sky-blue brand ground, line icon + short headline; the Live Activity shot ('Boards in 25 minutes') shows a concrete moment.
One word per headline in a Google colour (Shop from a screenshot); clean and specific, light on persuasion.
The feature name sits in a blue pill with its icon inside the headline ('Search what you see with [Lens]'), tying each caption to a visible UI element.
Mascot opener, then three-line small captions in English over dense UI.
Four raw dark screens with no captions.
Onboarding screens used as store screenshots: small grey text and 'Get started' buttons.
Bold verb + lighter object (Delete / Duplicate Photos) and a concrete number on every screen (Delete 20GB, 437MB > 2.9MB); proves the value but feels like a template.
A knitted-rope motif wraps every phone, warm cream/maroon palette, and copy with a voice ('Not degrees, a decision.', 'Cardigan or coat? One glance.', 'Heads-up, just like mom').
The data visualisations are beautiful enough to sell themselves; captions are small spec labels (50+ Interactive Maps).
'Label: specifics' headlines with the label in blue ('Exact rain timing: start to finish', 'No ads: hourly, 15 days, pollen'): instantly scannable and concrete.
Old raw screens with a carrier status bar and no captions.
Seasonal autumn photography behind the UI, bold 2-3 word headline + coloured specifics (15-day forecast for fall weekends & game days) and life-context use cases.
Strong storm-blue look and data cards popped out (Hurricane Milton wind speeds); headlines are feature names.
Credibility first (MORE THAN 12,000 LIVES SAVED) and a single user quote on the storm shot; captions are thin and long.
Thin centred captions in vague superlatives ('Delivering You the Most Hyper-Local Forecast on the Planet') on loud gradient backgrounds.
Raw 2016-era screens with a Carrier status bar and no captions; a library app that never told its own story.
Loud brand yellow, condensed caps headlines with a concrete sub-line ('the same day as Japan'); the manga covers carry it.
One verb per shot in big caps (UPLOAD, PREVIEW, TRACK) on black; clear for a utility, the tilted opener with a trophy is the weakest shot.
Line-drawn people above each phone and bold-keyword headlines naming real HR tasks (Review your time off balance); calm but small type.

Indie dev tool done right: mint brand colour, plain 3-4 word headlines naming exact jobs (Fix merge conflicts, Commit graph with search) over real code UI; the opener is an honest feature list for a pro audience.
Spec-label caps headlines (DEVICE and SENSOR Information) with small sub-paragraphs on a purple gradient; eight shots that look the same.
Consistent purple and verb-led headlines aimed at centre owners (Manage fast and secure check-in); 'The #1' and Shark Tank badge carry the opener.
Tiny serif captions on a photo of a keyboard and old phones; unreadable at search size.
Copy with rhythm and a point ('Every event. No hidden fees. Ever.', 'Track. Freeze. Save.', 'See it. Pick it. Done.'), a review shot and price-chart cards pulled out of the UI.
Cinematic dark set with sentence headlines about the viewer's role (Watch and vote on new projects); the mission line on shot 1 is vague.
Concrete numbers with footnotes (+25pts in your 1st month*, $3500 tradeline), underlined key figures; parachutes and 3D props are noisy.
Floating 3D gold coins, piggy bank and pastel gradients around tilted phones; the '$25 to $500' offer is clear but the set looks generated.
Brand red and the brand's condensed caps with a small overline ('GET IT AGAIN → YOUR "USUAL" FASTER'); 'Built from the buns up' is a good pun, the opener just announces the app.
Each headline is split above and below the phone ('ORDER AHEAD … AND AVOID THE LINE'), real food and people photography, hand-drawn arrows tying the shots together.
Quiet NYT editorial system: small serif sentence headlines on grey with real puzzles; very clear, a bit too quiet at search size.
Eight near-identical boards labelled only 'Level 15…50'; shows progression but no reason to play this one.
Real artwork does the selling; captions are small feature labels (Packed with Brushes, Layers, Blend Modes, and Masks).
White template with clear verb-led headlines (Remove backgrounds, Try on models) and real product results; clean but generic in look.
Small captions and tilted collages on mint; 'Your go-to app for all things fitness & wellness' fails the swap test.
Black, calm and premium with real health data; the thin Title-Case captions are hard to read and 'Your Personal Health Companion' is generic.
Four small-caption shots on blue, tilted opener with the app name; relies entirely on the membership brand.
Teal system with the key words in yellow (Make a Wishlist, Never Miss a Birthday); store logos and gift cards pop out of the frame; Title Case and laurels feel dated.
Newspaper-style serif headlines on white with real articles; tidy but mostly section names (US News, Lifestyle).
Economist red with its serif in sentence headlines that sound like the paper ('Go beyond breaking news in minutes', 'Make sense of the numbers'); every screen shows real journalism.
Pastel colour per shot with a highlighted key phrase (Track Baby's Growth); the fruit-size comparison on shot 1 is a lovable proof; headlines are feature labels.
Bold-keyword headlines (Track your baby's development) and a magnified 'Morning Sickness: what helps you?' callout; '#1 pregnancy app' opener is a claim, not a promise.
Bare setup screens with no captions; a hardware companion app that never says what it does.
Playful Gen-Z voice (SNOOP ON REPEATERS, FIND YOUR TUNE TWINS), stickers and emoji that belong to the product's own UI, two-tone caps on moody gradients from the album art.
A clear pay-at-the-pump journey, but every caption is a small two-line sentence on the same blue; nothing reads at search size.
Agency blue with short Title-Case jobs (Track Your Train in Real Time, Easy on Eyes at Night) over real timetables; clear, unremarkable.
Brand name and laurels on the first two shots, small captions and confetti shapes after; the AI-digest shot is the only differentiator and it's shot 4.
Small line icon + small two-line caption on white; calm but invisible at search size.
Strong results (before/after DIGI CAM, relight effects) on black; captions are small and the portraits lean on the AI-filter look.
White template with feature names (Speech Cleanup, AutoCut, Speed Curve) over real edits; reads like a feature list.
Indie planner with a soft pink system and lowercase two-weight headlines (your simple day planner, establish routines & habits) placed around the UI; awards and quotes used sparingly.
'One Chatbot, Endless Possibilities' and 'Generate Any Image' on dark glossy gradients with a cartoon AI portrait; the example prompts are concrete but the set is the AI-wrapper template.
Serif headlines with one italic word over sunset photography, the widget shown on a real lock screen and a shot of short user reviews; sincere, if a little stock-scenic.
Purple system with a short user quote under every headline and a whole testimonial shot; headlines themselves are category labels (Sleep Meditations).
Strong two-beat copy ('Find the Right Car. Not Just Any Car.', 'See How Reliable a Car Will Be. Before You Buy.') with the fox mascot; tilted phones and Title Case age it.
Concrete numbers (Earn $100 a year on average, 3,500+ stores, 22,000+ restaurants) and a wall of real retailer logos; small serif captions on deep purple.
Lowercase two-weight headlines (explore / the global village, without / language barrier) over real posts; airy but small at search size.
Cute pets and widgets in a pastel colour per shot, matching the couples/besties audience; busy, but every shot shows the real widget.
Blue topo-pattern ground, specific golfer jobs (Distances to the Pin on Every Hole, Leave Your Phone in the Cart) with watch and 3D green shots; Title Case throughout.
Betting app: neon-purple brand system with condensed caps and an offer opener; on-brand for the category, loud everywhere.
Conversational copy that runs across shots ('From outdoor adventures… to wine tastings', 'Travel hiccups? Cancel for free') with sticker circles and real people cut-outs on brand green.
Giant 'Right place / Right time' poster pair, then orange shots with concrete promises (Got your phone? Then you've got your tickets) and a real-review shot.
Small condensed caps sentences on mint across seven near-identical shots; the fox mascot is the only memorable thing.
Punchy two-weight caps (FAST SECURE PRIVATE, AD BLOCK BY DEFAULT, SYNC BROWSE CONTINUE) on soft brand gradients; clear but generic for a browser.
Short spoken headlines ('Your weekend. Full radar access.', 'Your weather. At a glance.') with hand-drawn arrows and labels pointing at the radar; every shot is one clear idea.
Spring photography behind the UI with event-based use cases (St. Patrick's Day parade, Easter picnic); caps headlines are small.
